messages:
Anna: quick thought 1: small "pin-bump" action via the deploy bot could save us minutes during noisy incidents. not a full rollback, just a safe nudge.

Devon: what exactly would it do? :thinking_face:

Anna: flow sketch: /pin-bump <svc> <rev> --reason "short reason" --ttl 60
- validate revision exists
- open ops PR that updates rollpointer/manifest
- set a default TTL (1h) and auto-unpin after ttl unless --keep provided
- include a dry-run preview option

Mike: manual rollback today is clunky: find manifest, run deployctl pin, push PR. easy to mess up under pressure. this would standardize it.

Liz: dry-run is a hard requirement for SRE. can we have /pin-bump --dry-run that shows the exact commands and PR diff?

Anna: yes. bot should respond with a preview: commands it will run, PR diff snippet, and a link to create the PR.

Sam: change-window safety: requests during a change window should require oncall ack or 2 approvals. bot can check calendar or a channel flag.

Devon: backend mock (POST payload):
```
POST /bot/pin-bump
payload: { "service": "api", "target": "v2026-03-21-rc3", "reason": "mitigate rate spike", "ttl_mins": 60 }
```
Bot steps: validation -> PR stub -> (optionally) apply pin -> watch metrics -> post status.

Mike: after the pin, bot should poll basic health signals and post a short summary: ok / suspect / revert-recommended. if revert recommended, ask for two-person confirm.

OpsBot: I will create PR #<n> in ops/rollpointer with the pin change. I will only auto-merge with 2 approvals and no active alerts.

Liz: auto-merge makes me nervous. maybe default is manual merge by oncall; auto-merge only if dry-run passed and 15m of quiet signals.

Anna: agreed, stricter auto-merge rules. default manual.

Sam: metrics to monitor: cpu, error-rate (5xx), p95 latency, frontend 5xx. keep it configurable per service.

Devon: small helper script for operators who prefer a single-pane view (tmux):
```
# scripts/tmux-pin-watch.sh
service=$1; rev=$2
tmux new-session -d -s pin-$service \\
  "tail -n 200 /var/log/$service/*.log" \; split-window -v "watch -n 10 deployctl status $service" \; split-window -h "watch -n 5 kubectl get pods -l service=$service"
```

Mike: that tmux view will cut down coordination noise during incidents.

Anna: UX notes: short confirmation modal in Slack with preview, explicit undo command (/pin-unwind <pr>) and a linkable PR. support --note-url to link incident writeups.

Devon: I'll prototype the pin-bump endpoint behind a feature flag and wire the dry-run + PR creation. aim to canary in staging.

Sam: I'll produce metric thresholds and a small read API for the bot to query signal windows.

Anna: follow-ups: implement backend + validation (Devon), define thresholds & change-window policy (Sam + Liz), UX + undo flows (Anna).

OpsBot: reminder: scheduled change window in ~2h. pin-bump requests during the window will require oncall ack.

Mike: filing follow-ups in GH (placeholder): https://github.com/redwood/ops/pulls

Anna: TL;DR: build /pin-bump (dry-run, TTL, PR stub, metrics watch, change-window checks, undo), plus a small tmux helper. volunteers: Devon + Sam. thanks :rocket:
